title: PostgreSQL Enterprise Substrate — Security, Privacy & Procurement Review

telemetry_operational_state_boundary.principle: Product telemetry opt-out must degrade adaptive product-learning behaviors, not break governance, auditability, enterprise evidence, projection invalidation, or operational correctness. Four distinct layers must not be conflated.

layer_1_product_telemetry.purpose: Remote or aggregated product-learning telemetry: UX optimization, agent-tool optimization, Ralph/orchestrator/subagent refinement, adaptive behavior, cross-org product intelligence.
layer_1_product_telemetry.opt_out_behavior: Disabling product telemetry removes: remote contribution, cross-user aggregate intelligence, hosted product-learning analytics, adaptive recommendations derived from telemetry, product optimization feedback loops. Adaptive product-learning behaviors visibly degrade.
layer_1_product_telemetry.opt_out_must_not: Disable receipt persistence, mutation receipts, release-gate decisions, schema validation records, export manifests, enterprise audit events, content-light incident investigation records, or Postgres operational substrate features.

layer_2_local_operational_observability.purpose: Local event logs, receipt metadata, trace metadata, projection invalidation, cockpit operational health, local diagnostics, and audit evidence. These are required product state/evidence for governed operation.
layer_2_local_operational_observability.opt_out_behavior: Local observability is NOT optional tracking — it is required for governed operation. It may only be explicitly disabled via a separate local_diagnostics setting (distinct from product telemetry consent).
layer_2_local_operational_observability.opt_out_must_not: Be disabled by product-telemetry opt-out. Must not be conflated with product telemetry.
layer_2_local_operational_observability.cockpit_status: local_observability_degraded (only when local_diagnostics is explicitly disabled)

layer_3_enterprise_audit_evidence_substr.purpose: Postgres-backed audit trails, enterprise_audit_event, mutation_receipt, release_gate_decision, receipt_envelope, export_manifest, schema_registry, and artifact_registry.
layer_3_enterprise_audit_evidence_substr.opt_out_behavior: These must continue to function even when product telemetry is disabled. Enterprise audit/evidence cannot silently stop refreshing because telemetry was disabled. Disabling product telemetry must not weaken auditability, compliance evidence, incident investigation, or governance gates.
layer_3_enterprise_audit_evidence_substr.enterprise_mode_requirement: Enterprise audit/evidence tables remain mandatory in enterprise mode regardless of telemetry consent state.
layer_3_enterprise_audit_evidence_substr.cockpit_status: enterprise_substrate_unavailable (only when Postgres is configured but unreachable)

layer_4_local_adaptive_ux.purpose: Adaptive product-learning behaviors: suggested tool sequences, Ralph mission-candidate ranking, orchestrator subagent refinement.
layer_4_local_adaptive_ux.opt_out_behavior: When product telemetry is disabled, adaptive behavior can visibly degrade — adaptive recommendations may disappear, ranking quality may decrease.
layer_4_local_adaptive_ux.cockpit_status: product_telemetry_disabled (surface as info, not as error)

cockpit_three_state_model.description: Cockpit must surface three separately distinguishable states, never conflated into a single 'degraded' label.
cockpit_three_state_model.state_1: product_telemetry_disabled — product-learning features are offline. Governance, audit, receipts, and operational health are unaffected.
cockpit_three_state_model.state_2: local_observability_degraded — local event collection is reduced (only when local_diagnostics is explicitly disabled). Audit/enterprise records may still be intact.
cockpit_three_state_model.state_3: enterprise_substrate_unavailable — Postgres is configured but unreachable. This is fail-closed. Cockpit shows 'Enterprise substrate unavailable'.

audit_evidence_continuity_guarantee.text: Disabling product telemetry must never disable receipt persistence, mutation receipts, release-gate decisions, schema validation records, export manifests, enterprise audit events, or content-light incident investigation records. Enterprise audit/evidence tables (enterprise_audit_event, mutation_receipt, release_gate_decision, receipt_envelope, export_manifest, schema_registry, artifact_registry) must continue to append and queryable even when product telemetry consent is withdrawn.
audit_evidence_continuity_guarantee.enforcement: Telemetry consent state (opt-in/opt-out) governs product_telemetry layer only. It has no effect on Postgres INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT paths for audit/evidence tables. Application-level guard: if telemetry consent is false, skip product_telemetry writes but always execute audit/evidence writes.
audit_evidence_continuity_guarantee.test_required: Disable product telemetry consent. Verify that receipt_envelope INSERT succeeds. Verify that mutation_receipt INSERT succeeds. Verify that release_gate_decision INSERT succeeds. Verify that enterprise_audit_event INSERT succeeds. Verify that export_manifest INSERT succeeds.

what_may_go_into_postgres: Receipt envelope metadata (receipt_kind, session_id, actor_kind, subject_kind, decision_kind, created_at, SHA256 hashes)
Session lifecycle events (event_name, session_id, sequence, created_at, duration_ms)
Coordination metadata (lease_id, session_id, task_id, status, path_hashes, ttl_seconds, expires_at)
Schema registry metadata (schema_id, schema_version, schema_path, content_sha256, title, description)
Release gate decisions (gate_name, decision_kind, severity, status, reasons[], evidence refs)
Findings metadata (finding_id, dedupe_key, kind, severity, status, title, description)
Provider operating picture metadata (provider, trust_tier, health_status, capability matrix — no tokens)
Tool invocation metadata (tool_name, status, latency_ms, receipt_sha256 — no args or outputs)
Telemetry aggregates (counts, rates, percentile latencies — no raw events)
Audit events (event_kind, actor_id, action, target_id, before/after SHA256, reason)
Export manifests (table_name, row_count, export_sha256, source_sha256 — no exported data)
User preferences and consent state (preference keys, boolean flags, consent timestamps — no PII)
what_must_never_go_into_postgres: Raw LLM prompts — may contain proprietary code, secrets accidentally pasted, business logic
Raw LLM completions — may contain generated code, reasoning, potential sensitive content
Raw file contents — repository source code, configuration files, private data
Raw stdout/stderr from tool execution — may contain secrets, file paths, proprietary output
Raw git diffs and patches — may contain proprietary code, file paths, secrets
API keys and credentials — provider API keys, OAuth tokens, GitHub tokens
OAuth access tokens — Google Drive, GitHub, any OAuth provider tokens
Private repository file paths outside the project workspace
Raw email addresses, domain names, calendar titles, drive filenames from Google Workspace integration
Search query terms that may contain proprietary keywords or code
Symbol codec raw bodies — source code snippets from tree-sitter parsing
Debug packet contents — may contain any of the above
Mission context packet raw contents — may contain compressed code snippets
Local inference benchmark prompt/response pairs — may contain evaluation code

enforcement_mechanism.layer_1_application: All Postgres adapters validate payloads against content-light schemas before INSERT. pydantic+jsonschema validation at Postgres boundary.
enforcement_mechanism.layer_2_database: CHECK constraints on all JSONB columns validate against forbidden key patterns (token, secret, private_key, raw_prompt, raw_completion, file_content, diff, patch). INSERT triggers raise exception on forbidden content.
enforcement_mechanism.layer_3_testing: Content-light regression tests: insert known forbidden payloads and verify constraint rejection. Every table with JSONB column must have corresponding content-light enforcement tests.

content_light_enforcement.definition: Content-light means: no raw file contents, no prompts, no completions, no stdout/stderr, no diffs, no patches, no secrets, no API keys, no private file paths, no PII (email, name, domain), no private repository content.
content_light_enforcement.allowed_fields_pattern: event metadata (name, timestamp, sequence, session_id), SHA256 hashes, status enums, counts/aggregates, latency/duration, error kinds (not messages with code), tool names (not args), schema IDs, path hashes (salted SHA256 of paths, not raw paths).
postgres_enforcement: Generated columns extract only allowlisted fields from JSONB payloads
CHECK constraints validate JSONB key sets against content-light allowlist
INSERT trigger: enumerate all keys in incoming JSONB payload, reject any key matching forbidden pattern
Materialized views only aggregate from typed columns, never from raw JSONB payloads
Role-based access: analyst role cannot query JSONB payload columns — only typed generated columns and materialized views

operational_tables.event_log: 30-day online. Monthly partitions exported as gzipped JSONL to cold storage. Cold storage retained 1 year.
operational_tables.cockpit_ui_state: Per-session ephemeral. Deleted on session close.

permanent_tables.artifact_validation: 90-day retention for operational querying. Export to cold storage for compliance.
permanent_tables.receipt_envelope: 90-day retention for operational querying. Indefinite retention in canonical files.
permanent_tables.finding: Indefinite retention. Resolved findings move to cold storage partition after 90 days.
permanent_tables.mutation_receipt: Indefinite retention for mutation audit trail.
permanent_tables.export_manifest: Indefinite retention for export audit trail.

retention_policy.cold_storage: .build/rig-relay/archive/ — gzipped JSONL exports. Duplicated to ~/.rig/relay/archive/ for user-global. Always restorable from canonical artifacts.

export_delete_story.export: Every Postgres table has a corresponding export function that produces JSON/JSONL/CSV artifacts matching the canonical artifact format. Export manifests verify SHA256 equivalence between Postgres data and exported artifacts.
export_delete_story.delete: Individual rows are NEVER deleted from audit trail tables (enterprise_audit_event, mutation_receipt, release_gate_decision). Operational tables (event_log, trace_event) have partition-based retention — old partitions are detached, exported to cold storage, then dropped. No soft-delete patterns — rows are either present or exported-then-purged.
export_delete_story.gdpr_right_to_erasure: Enterprise audit events link to pseudonymous session IDs, not personally identifiable information. If tenant-level erasure is required, entire tenant partition is exported then dropped. Tenant audit log records the erasure event.

database_roles.privileges: SUPERUSER equivalent: CREATE DATABASE, CREATE ROLE, all DDL operations. Used for migration execution and schema management. Never used by application code.
database_roles.access_control: Password-authenticated via pg_hba.conf. Local Unix socket only.

database_roles.privileges: CRUD on all operational tables. Can INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT but cannot DROP, ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, or manage roles. Application service account.
database_roles.access_control: md5/scram-sha-256 authenticated. Used by Rig Relay application.

database_roles.privileges: SELECT only on content-light materialized views. Cannot query base tables or JSONB columns directly. Used by cockpit dashboard queries.
database_roles.access_control: md5/scram-sha-256 authenticated. Used by cockpit analytics backend.

database_roles.privileges: SELECT only on enterprise_audit_event and export_manifest. Cannot see operational data. Used by compliance/audit tooling.
database_roles.access_control: Separate password. Read-only. Access logged as audit events.

admin_access_model.local_vs_enterprise: In local mode, rig_relay_admin is the default role with password 'local_only' (only accepts local Unix socket connections). In enterprise mode, roles are provisioned by the tenant admin with secure passwords managed via the credential store.

audit_event_types: admin_action — schema migration, role creation, backup operation
permission_change — RLS policy change, role grant/revoke
export_operation — export manifest creation, cold storage archival
incident_investigation_path: 1. Query enterprise_audit_event for time window and affected tenant/actor
2. Cross-reference event_log for session activity during the incident
3. Query receipt_envelope for tool invocations during affected sessions
4. Query coordination_lease for path reservations overlapping affected files
5. Export affected partition to analysts for offline investigation
6. Replay canonical artifacts to verify Postgres records match source-of-truth

backup: Full backup: pg_dump -Fc (custom format) daily. Stored in .build/rig-relay/backups/.
WAL archiving: pg_receivewal for point-in-time recovery (enterprise mode only).
Canonical artifacts are the ultimate backup — all Postgres data can be rebuilt from JSON/JSONL/CSV source artifacts via Phase 4 replay process.
Backup encrypts with age encryption using Rig Relay's attestation key.
restore: Option 1 (fast): pg_restore from daily backup. Verify SHA256 against canonical artifacts.
Option 2 (slow but authoritative): Replay canonical artifacts through Postgres adapters to rebuild all operational tables. Run Phase 4 equivalence verification.
Restore is tested monthly in Phase 7 procurement validation.

local_vs_hosted_enterprise_boundary.local_mode: Postgres runs locally (brew install postgresql@16, or bundled via pyinstaller with embedded postgres). No network exposure. No RLS. No tenant isolation. Single user. Backup via pg_dump to local filesystem.
local_vs_hosted_enterprise_boundary.enterprise_mode: Postgres connection string configured via RIG_RELAY_POSTGRES_DSN env var or config TOML. RLS enabled. Tenant isolation active. Connection pooling with pgbouncer recommended. WAL archiving to S3/GCS. Access controlled via pg_hba.conf with scram-sha-256.
boundary_assertions: Local mode never enables RLS or tenant isolation
Enterprise mode never accepts local-only authentication
Postgres DSN is never hardcoded in source or committed to repo
Connection string validation: must not be localhost in enterprise mode (anti-localhost-pivot protection)

procurement_readiness_implications.capability_gain: Postgres enables SOC 2 Type II audit trails, role-based access for procurement review, automated backup/restore for BCDR compliance, tenant isolation for multi-enterprise deployments.
remaining_gaps: No secrets rotation mechanism for Postgres credentials (deferred to credential store hardening)
No automated failover for Postgres in enterprise mode (deferred to hosted deployment)
No encryption-at-rest for Postgres data files (deferred to enterprise deployment with LUKS/KMS)
No connection pooling for enterprise mode (recommend pgbouncer in deployment docs, not bundled)
compliance_evidence_artifacts: audit_trail: enterprise_audit_event table + exported JSONL artifacts
access_control: pg_authid + pg_roles information_schema views + RLS policy definitions
backup_restore: export_manifest table + backup script logs
data_retention: partition management logs + cold storage export manifests
content_light_guarantee: CHECK constraint definitions + constraint violation logs + redaction test reports
